structured_concern: Owner reports: Truck shakes when I'm cruising around 45, feels like driving over rumble strips. Occurs at 40-50 mph; while cruising, light throttle; engine warm. Frequency: sometimes. Started: about 2 weeks ago, gradual.

likely_causes.name: Torque converter clutch shudder
likely_causes.why: Shudder that only shows up warm at a steady, light-throttle cruise is the classic converter-clutch pattern.
diy_checks: Check transmission fluid level and condition if your vehicle has a dipstick (red/pink and not burnt-smelling is good).
Note the exact speed it happens. If a light tap of the brake (without slowing) or a slight throttle change makes it stop instantly, that points to the converter clutch.
Scan for codes, including pending codes.
likely_causes.difficulty_label: Advanced - special tools or lifting the vehicle
likely_causes.pro_when: Fluid service or software updates often need a shop scan tool. Internal converter problems are a shop job.

likely_causes.name: Engine misfire (plugs, coils, or injector)
likely_causes.why: Shaking with stumbling or a check engine light most often comes from ignition parts.
diy_checks: Scan for codes. P0301-P0308 tell you which cylinder.
If one cylinder is misfiring and your engine has coil-on-plug, swap that coil with a neighbor. If the misfire follows the coil, replace the coil.
Pull and inspect the spark plug in that cylinder. Look for oil, cracks, or a worn electrode.
likely_causes.pro_when: If the check engine light is flashing, stop driving: unburned fuel can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter.

likely_causes.name: Driveline, tire, or wheel balance vibration
likely_causes.why: Vibration that follows road speed rather than engine load usually comes from the tires, wheels, or driveshaft.
diy_checks: Look for uneven tire wear, bulges, or missing wheel weights.
Check whether the vibration depends on speed (same at any throttle) or on load. Speed-only usually means tires, balance, or the driveshaft.
With the vehicle safely on jack stands, check u-joints for play by twisting the driveshaft by hand.
likely_causes.pro_when: Tire balancing needs a shop machine. Any play in the u-joints or a wobbling tire should be fixed before highway driving.

needs_more_info: Can you read the codes? Many parts stores scan for free, or a basic OBD2 reader costs about $20-30.
